text:
A prisoner killed the Soham murderer Ian Huntley with a heavy metal bar in a “cold-blooded” attack that had been planned weeks in advance, a court heard.
Jurors were told that Anthony Russell, 44, repeatedly hit the 52-year-old over the head in the attack at the high-security HMP Frankland, near Durham.
Matthew Bean KC, prosecuting, told jurors at Newcastle crown court that they may feel no sympathy for the Soham killer, who murdered Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman in 2002, but the case was not about his “appalling actions” but the manner in which he had died.
Russell denies a single count of murder.
Bean said: “At shortly after 9am on 26 February 2026, the prosecution say that the defendant in this trial, Anthony Russell, murdered Ian Huntley, by striking him repeatedly to the head with a heavy metal bar. The prosecution case is that this was a cold-blooded murder that had been planned weeks in advance of its execution.
“It happened in a prison, HMP Frankland, where both Anthony Russell and Ian Huntley were serving prisoners. At the time, both men were serving sentences of life imprisonment for offences of murder.
“The defendant, Anthony Russell, you will hear, had previously been convicted of the murder of three people, these offences having taken place in October 2020. The name of the man he killed, Ian Huntley, will be known to many, if not all of you.
“He had been convicted of the murder of two girls, Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman, that took place in the village of Soham in Cambridgeshire in August 2002. These were offences that, for entirely understandable reasons, aroused feelings of disgust and anger.
“Due to the nature of his offences, you may feel little or no sympathy for what happened to him. More than that, the prosecution do not ask for sympathy.
“Ultimately, this case is not about the appalling actions of Ian Huntley during his life, but the manner of his death. The prosecution well understands the emotions that may be stirred during this trial.
“It is essential, however, to be true to your oath or affirmation, to put emotion to one side, to try this case on the evidence and the evidence alone, and to come to verdicts based on that evidence.”
Bean told jurors the two murderers were held on A wing at the high-security prison and there had been “tension” between them in the months leading up to the killing.
About a year earlier, in March 2025, prison staff witnessed an argument between them in which they threatened one another and had to be separated.
They later agreed with staff that nothing further would happen, the court heard.
About 10 months later, Russell was seen with a black eye, and told staff he had fallen.
Bean said: “Some members of staff believed, however, that someone had assaulted him and you will hear some evidence during the trial that indicates that it may have been caused by Ian Huntley.”
Those incidents were the only two issues between the men in the prison records, the court heard.
The trial continues.
